title: Chicago violent crime: rates, clusters and regions
blurb: Chicago recorded about 80,000 violent crimes in 2024, and they are far from evenly spread. This case compares the rate across the city's 77 community areas, asks whether high-rate areas sit next to each other, and groups the city into regions with similar rates.

steps.label: Rates by community area
steps.prompt: Count the 2024 violent crimes in each Chicago community area, compute the rate per 1,000 residents and map it as a choropleth. What is the citywide rate, and which community area has the highest rate?

steps.label: Are the rates clustered?
steps.prompt: Test whether those rates are spatially clustered with global Moran's I (queen contiguity, row-standardised weights), then map the local (LISA) clusters: high-high, low-low and the outliers.

steps.label: Six crime regions
steps.prompt: Group the 77 community areas into 6 contiguous regions with similar violent crime rates using SKATER. Map the regions and give each one's community areas, population and mean rate.

title: Schools within a mile of a site
blurb: A development site in the Chicago Loop and the schools around it. The case asks which schools are within a mile of the site and which one is closest.

steps.label: Count and nearest
steps.prompt: How many schools are within 1 mile of the site at 41.8827 N, 87.6233 W? Which one is nearest, and how far is it in metres?

steps.label: Show it on the map
steps.prompt: Show the site, its 1-mile buffer and the schools inside it on the map.

title: Incidents per 1,000 residents by zone
blurb: Incidents recorded across nine zones with very different populations. The zone with the most incidents is not the one where an incident is most likely per resident.

steps.label: Rates by zone
steps.prompt: Compute each zone's incident rate per 1,000 residents. Which zone has the highest rate, and what is it?

steps.label: Map the rates
steps.prompt: Map the rate per 1,000 residents for each zone as a choropleth.

title: Fastest route on a road network
blurb: A small grid of Chicago streets, each with its own speed. The shortest way between two intersections is not the fastest, and the case also asks how far you can get in two minutes.

steps.label: Fastest travel time
steps.prompt: What is the fastest travel time in minutes on this road network from the intersection at 41.87408° N, 87.65075° W to the one at 41.89222° N, 87.62683° W? How many intersections, counting the start, can be reached within 2 minutes of it?

steps.label: Show the route
steps.prompt: Show the fastest route on the map.

title: Where to put two facilities
blurb: Forty neighbourhoods with known populations and eight possible sites for two new facilities. The case finds the pair of sites that keeps people closest to a facility overall.

steps.label: Choose the sites
steps.prompt: Choose the 2 candidate sites that minimise the total population-weighted straight-line distance from each demand point to its nearest chosen site. Which two sites, and what is that total in person-kilometres?

steps.label: Map the service areas
steps.prompt: Map the demand points coloured by the chosen site that serves each one, and mark the two chosen sites.

title: Land under a 5 m flood
blurb: An elevation model of a low-lying coastal tile, with a few cells of missing data. The case asks how much land lies at or below 5 m if the water rises that far.

steps.label: Flooded area
steps.prompt: If water rises to 5 m, how many hectares of this coast are at or below that level? Treat it as a simple bathtub: every cell at or below 5 m counts.

steps.label: Show the flood
steps.prompt: Show the flooded cells on the map.

title: Vegetation change from two scenes
blurb: Two satellite scenes of the same area, from 2020 and 2024. The case measures how green the area was on each date and how much of it lost vegetation in between.

steps.label: NDVI and loss
steps.prompt: Compute NDVI for 2020 and 2024. What is the mean NDVI on each date, and how many hectares lost more than 0.2 NDVI between them?

steps.label: Map the loss
steps.prompt: Map where NDVI fell by more than 0.2 between the two dates.

title: Site suitability from three layers
blurb: Three aligned layers for one area: slope, distance to the nearest road, and land cover. The case finds the land that is flat, near a road and not water or wetland, and the single best spot.

steps.label: Score the cells
steps.prompt: A cell is suitable if its slope is under 8 degrees, its road distance is at most 500 m, and its land cover is not water or wetland. Score each suitable cell as 0.5*(1 - slope/8) + 0.5*(1 - distance/500). What is the total suitable area in hectares, and what are the centre coordinates of the highest-scoring cell?

steps.label: Map the score
steps.prompt: Map the suitability score.

title: Aftershocks of the 2019 Ridgecrest earthquake
blurb: In July 2019 a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck near Ridgecrest, California, followed by thousands of aftershocks. The case counts those in the following week within 25 km and maps them by magnitude.

steps.label: Count the aftershocks
steps.prompt: What was the magnitude of the largest event in the July 2019 Ridgecrest sequence? How many events occurred within 7 days after it and within 25 km of its epicentre, and how many of those were magnitude 4 or greater?

steps.label: Map them
steps.prompt: Map the aftershocks within 25 km and 7 days, sized by magnitude, with the mainshock marked.

title: Measuring area and distance correctly
blurb: Two measurements with nothing to upload: the area of Champaign County, Illinois, whose boundary the agent fetches itself, and the distance from Trafalgar Square in London to Notre-Dame in Paris.

steps.label: Area and distance
steps.prompt: What is the area of Champaign County, Illinois, in square kilometres? And what is the great-circle distance in km between Trafalgar Square, London (51.5080 N, 0.1281 W) and Notre-Dame de Paris (48.8530 N, 2.3499 E)?
